subject: Art and Culture
sub_topic: Major stupas — Sanchi, Bharhut, Amaravati, Sarnath

concepts.name: Sanchi Stupa: Chronological Development and Patronage
key_dimensions: Evolution from Mauryan (Ashoka) to Shunga to Satavahana periods - structural additions
Specific contributions: Ashoka's original stupa vs Shunga's gateways (toranas) and railings
UNESCO World Heritage status (1989) and conservation efforts by John Marshall
Comparison with other stupas: Only major stupa NOT at a site directly associated with Buddha's life

concepts.name: Sanchi Stupa: Architectural Components and Symbolism
key_dimensions: Anda (hemispherical dome), Harmika (square railing), Chhatravali (three-tiered umbrella) - symbolic meanings
Four elaborately carved toranas (gateways) - orientation and iconographic themes on each
Vedika (railing) with lotus medallions - distinction between stone and wooden prototypes
Pradakshina patha (circumambulatory path) - ritual significance and architectural layout

concepts.name: Sanchi Stupa: Sculptural Narratives and Aniconism
key_dimensions: Jataka tales depicted on toranas - specific stories like Chaddanta, Mahakapi, Vessantara
Aniconic representation of Buddha through symbols: Bodhi tree, wheel, footprints, empty throne
Yaksha-Yakshi figures and their pre-Buddhist folk tradition integration
Comparison with Bharhut: Sanchi's more evolved sculptural style and deeper relief work

concepts.name: Bharhut Stupa: Discovery, Current Status and Historical Significance
key_dimensions: Discovery by Alexander Cunningham (1873) - current dispersal of remains (Indian Museum Kolkata, other museums)
Dating to Shunga period (2nd century BCE) - inscriptional evidence and Brahmi inscriptions
Distinction: Most extensively labeled stupa with donor inscriptions providing social history
Comparison with Sanchi: Bharhut's railings are earlier but stupa itself largely destroyed

concepts.name: Bharhut Stupa: Sculptural Style and Narrative Technique
key_dimensions: Low relief (bas-relief) sculpture - primitive/archaic style compared to Sanchi
Extensive labeling of scenes in Brahmi script - educational purpose and identification
Jataka and Avadana stories with textual labels - specific examples like Vidhurapandita Jataka
Medallion format on railings depicting previous Buddhas and Bodhi trees of 24 Buddhas

concepts.name: Amaravati Stupa: Dynastic Patronage and Chronology
key_dimensions: Satavahana patronage (200 BCE - 200 CE) - longest construction period among major stupas
Three major phases of construction and sculptural additions
Ikshvaku dynasty contributions in later phase (3rd century CE)
Current state: Largely destroyed, remains in Government Museum Chennai and British Museum

concepts.name: Amaravati Stupa: Architectural Innovations and Layout
key_dimensions: Mahachaitya (great stupa) with elaborate ayaka platforms - unique to Amaravati school
Five ayaka pillars on each platform - their symbolic and architectural significance
Larger pradakshina patha with elaborate sculptural panels
Comparison with Sanchi: Amaravati's more complex ground plan and decorative scheme

concepts.name: Amaravati School: Sculptural Style and Iconographic Evolution
key_dimensions: Transition from aniconism to anthropomorphic Buddha representation (earliest examples)
Narrative friezes in dynamic composition - 'Amaravati style' characteristics
White marble limestone with greenish tinge - material distinction from other stupas
Influence on Southeast Asian art - Sri Lanka, Thailand, Indonesia connections

concepts.name: Amaravati Stupa: Thematic Representations and Innovations
key_dimensions: Depiction of stupa itself in relief panels - meta-representation providing architectural evidence
Life of Buddha in continuous narrative style - birth to mahaparinirvana
Kalachakra (Wheel of Time) representations - cosmological symbolism
Comparison with earlier stupas: More emphasis on Buddha's biography than Jatakas

concepts.name: Sarnath Stupa: Historical and Religious Significance
key_dimensions: Location significance: Site of Buddha's first sermon (Dhammachakkapravartana)
Dhamek Stupa - Gupta period construction (5th-6th century CE) over earlier Mauryan structure
Ashoka's pillar at Sarnath - Lion Capital as national emblem (separate from stupa)
Distinction: Only major stupa site with continuous Buddhist presence into medieval period

concepts.name: Dhamek Stupa: Architectural Features and Uniqueness
key_dimensions: Cylindrical shape with stone and brick construction - different from hemispherical stupas
Geometric and floral patterns in stone bands - Gupta period decorative style
Height (43.6 m) and diameter (28.3 m) specifications
Absence of elaborate gateways unlike Sanchi - simpler architectural approach

concepts.name: Comparative Chronology: Stupa Development Phases
key_dimensions: Mauryan phase (3rd century BCE): Original cores at Sanchi, Sarnath
Shunga phase (2nd-1st century BCE): Bharhut railings, Sanchi enlargement and toranas
Satavahana-Ikshvaku phase (1st-3rd century CE): Amaravati peak, Sanchi final additions
Gupta phase (4th-6th century CE): Sarnath's Dhamek Stupa reconstruction

concepts.name: Regional Schools and Stylistic Variations
key_dimensions: Mathura vs Amaravati schools - anthropomorphic Buddha representation differences
North Indian (Sanchi, Bharhut, Sarnath) vs South Indian (Amaravati) architectural features
Material usage: Sandstone (North) vs Limestone (South) - impact on sculptural style
Iconographic preferences: Jataka emphasis (North) vs Buddha biography (South)

concepts.name: Stupa Symbolism and Buddhist Cosmology
key_dimensions: Stupa as representation of Buddhist universe - anda as cosmic egg, yasti as world axis
Directional symbolism of four toranas - association with four great events of Buddha's life
Number symbolism: Three chhatras (Triratna), four gateways (four noble truths)
Relic worship and dhatu-garbha (relic chamber) - archaeological evidence from excavations

concepts.name: Inscriptional Evidence and Social History
key_dimensions: Donor inscriptions revealing social composition - monks, nuns, laity, guilds, women
Bharhut's extensive labeling vs Sanchi's minimal inscriptions - implications for literacy
Evidence of trade guilds and merchant patronage - economic history insights
Regional languages and scripts: Brahmi inscriptions providing linguistic evidence

concepts.name: Aniconic vs Iconic Representation: Chronological Transition
key_dimensions: Early phase (Bharhut, early Sanchi): Strict aniconism with symbols only
Transitional phase (late Sanchi, early Amaravati): Gradual introduction of human form
Later phase (Amaravati, Sarnath): Full anthropomorphic representation
Theological and artistic reasons for transition - Mahayana influence debate

concepts.name: Conservation and Archaeological Discoveries
key_dimensions: Alexander Cunningham's role: Discovery of Bharhut and Sarnath excavations
John Marshall's conservation at Sanchi (1912-1919) - restoration controversies
Colin Mackenzie's documentation of Amaravati (1816) - early British archaeological interest
Current UNESCO status and ASI management - preservation challenges

concepts.name: Toranas (Gateways): Iconography and Orientation
key_dimensions: Sanchi's four toranas: Specific themes on each (Eastern - Buddha's life events, Southern - previous births, etc.)
Architectural evolution from wooden prototypes - mortise and tenon joints in stone
Sculptural programs: Upper architraves vs vertical posts - hierarchical arrangement
Comparison: Sanchi's elaborate toranas vs absence at Sarnath and destroyed at Bharhut

concepts.name: Influence and Legacy: Pan-Asian Buddhist Architecture
key_dimensions: Amaravati's influence on Southeast Asian stupas - Borobudur, Anuradhapura connections
Sanchi as prototype for later Indian stupas - structural template
Transmission of architectural ideas via trade routes and missionary activities
Modern revival: Dhamek Stupa at Sarnath, Deekshabhoomi at Nagpur inspired by ancient models

concepts.name: UPSC Trap Areas: Specific Distinctions and Exceptions
key_dimensions: Only Sanchi has complete surviving toranas; Bharhut and Amaravati toranas are lost/fragmented
Sarnath's Dhamek Stupa is cylindrical, not hemispherical like others
Amaravati is the only major stupa with ayaka platforms and pillars
Bharhut has most extensive labeling; Sanchi has minimal inscriptions despite elaborate sculpture
Only Amaravati shows clear transition from aniconic to iconic Buddha representation on same monument
